# PR body — P26.17 (robots non-gating, GL-GATE-08 + refused-source re-sweep)

> Stacked on `devin/p26-16-rights-batch` (PR #108). Ticket:
> `docs/tickets/P26.17__robots-non-gating.md` (SOURCES.16).
> Run ledger: `docs/build/runs/P26.17.md`. ADR:
> `docs/adr/ADR-088-robots-verdicts-recorded-never-enforced-gl-gate-08.md`.

## What this lands

**Executes the operator's recorded GL-GATE-08 disposition** (LEDGER §
GATE DECISIONS, 2026-09-18): *disregard robots entirely — robots verdicts
stop gating fetches*. The probe still runs and the RFC 9309 §2.3.1.4
verdict is still recorded per host (ADR-087's classification layer is
kept verbatim — `retrieved` / `no_policy_4xx` / `unretrievable`), but a
`Disallow` verdict or an unretrievable policy **no longer refuses** the
fetch. Every fetch that proceeds despite a non-grant verdict is marked
`robots_disregarded` — per-URL rows on `PoliteFetcher`, the
`conduct_decisions` outcome, and the fetch record's new
`robots_disregarded` field — so a claim's provenance says the fetch
ignored a refusal. The weakened never-bypassed audit property is
compensated by making the disregard first-class data, never silent.

**Honest failures stay honest.** A transport-level failure on a
now-attempted host records an `unreachable` disappearance (new
`FAILING_STATUSES` member) instead of crashing the run; a WAF/401/403/
challenge stays `access_restricted` and `ChallengeEncountered` still
surfaces — **no challenge is defeated, no identity rotated, no CAPTCHA
solved** (SIG-INGEST-013). `RobotsDisallowed`/`RobotsUnretrievable` are
retained for record-vocabulary compatibility and non-standard fetchers;
the exit-6 `politeness_refusal` mapping survives for that compat path.
